programme.title: Hidden Lives
programme.desc: Samantha Little explores an extremely mucky pre-wedding ritual popular in the north of Scotland. Originating from an ancient custom of rubbing soot into the feet, the modern blackening is a very different affair and can be a wild and riotous occasion. The engaged couple are kidnapped and are `gunked', by friends and family, who use all manner of disgusting substances, including fermented dog food, rotten eggs and even fish guts.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian and Calum tackle Beechgrove's hedges after checking carefully for bird nest activity. Brian offers advice on how to care for common houseplants.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: It's the adventure escape category, and the Oliver family are tasked with rating the very best active getaways that Scotland has to offer. They take a trip to remote Doune Knoydart, which is only accessible by boat or a two-day hike across the mountains, Loch Ken Eco Bothies in Dumfries and Galloway, which boasts its own activity centre, and Eagle Brae, an eco-log cabin village set in an 8,000-acre estate in the heart of the Highlands.

programme.title: Granite Harbour

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Alan kicks off the dog benefit while Michelle's family watches from the audience. Meanwhile, Daphne shares her Icelandic plans with Alan, though she still grapples with how to break the news to Darren.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
